description: Automerge is the default posture here, not the exception. This repo is a design catalog with no downstream consumers: nothing depends on its artifacts, so a bad bump costs a revert, not a broken release. What stops a bad bump reaching main is the `Protect Main` ruleset — CI (build + discovery, unit tests, ktfmtCheck, catalog spec, catalog spec) is required, and `platformAutomerge` hands the merge to GitHub's own auto-merge, which only fires once those checks pass. Set the ruleset up with `scripts/setup-repo-protection.sh`; without it, automerge silently degrades to merging as soon as Renovate can, which is not what any of this intends.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. A major on Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform or the preview toolchain changes what the catalog renders, and the render is the product — a human looks at the visual diff before it lands. Also hold a major for two weeks so the ecosystem's first round of regressions surfaces on someone else's CI.

Wear Compose and the mobile Compose BOM decide how every sticker in the catalog is laid out, and the render is the product — so they land as one PR whose visual diff is the review, not on automerge. Glance Wear is in the group because it is the third member of the Remote trio (AGENTS.md): it shares a `remote-creation*` base with `compose-remote` and `wear-compose-remote`, so a bump of it alone skews the trio and fails in the player at render time (#652).

Horologist is the catalog's SECOND component library (see AGENTS.md) and it ships its artifacts as one release — media-ui-material3, auth-composables-material3, compose-layout, images-base and the models they take all move together, and a skew between them is a compile error at best. Group them into one PR. Not automerged, for the same reason Compose is not: these draw the media player, the sign-in screens and the fast-scrolling list, and the render is the product — a human reads the visual diff. They are on an alpha line, so expect the diff to be real.

Toolchain and CI plumbing — the Gradle wrapper, the GitHub Actions pins and the pinned Node version. These are judged entirely by whether CI passes, which is the one thing automerge already waits for, so batch them into a single weekly PR rather than one PR per action. Deliberately BEFORE the compose-ai-tools rule, which re-claims its own action ref out of this batch — that pin travels with the Gradle coords, not with the weekly plumbing.

Every ee.schimke.composeai MODULE coordinate is held back, the compose-preview daemon BOM included. Since the BOM fix, the modules in gradle/libs.versions.toml are versionless and resolve through their line's BOM (`platform(...)` in every module that uses them), because compose-preview-daemon and compose-ui-builder publish only the modules that changed in a release: a per-module pin at the release version 404s the first time a release skips a module (data-preview-overrides-runtime 3.13.0 does not exist while preview-annotations 3.13.0 does), which is #199, #347 and #637 again. The daemon BOM's version (`composePreviewDaemon`) must equal the daemon release the compose-preview plugin BAKES. The daemon always releases before the plugin that bakes it, and Renovate cannot read the baked value, so an independent BOM update would run ahead of the plugin, and grouping or minimumGroupSize would still raise it to the latest daemon rather than the baked one. The BOM therefore moves only in the plugin's PR, set by hand to the value :verifyComposePreviewDaemonAlignment (root build.gradle.kts, run before every compose-preview module compiles) reports. This also stops Renovate looking up the synthetic `ui-builder-renderer-sdk-source` coordinate, which is never on Maven. The plugin marker (`ee.schimke.composeai.preview`, no colon after `composeai`) is not matched, and the UI-builder BOM is re-enabled by the last rule.

LAST-BUT-ONE ON PURPOSE, below the CI-toolchain rule: Renovate applies packageRules in order and the LAST match wins, and while this rule sat above that one the pinned `compose-ai-tools` action ref, a github-actions dependency, was pulled back out into the weekly batch and the two halves of one release drifted apart (compose-ai-tools#4220 found the pin three releases behind the Gradle coords). compose-ai-tools ships the preview CLI, the ee.schimke.composeai.preview plugin and the reusable CI actions/workflows as ONE release, so the plugin marker and the pinned action refs move together in ONE PR and can never skew apart; a skew breaks preview discovery outright. When the new plugin bakes a different daemon, that PR fails :verifyComposePreviewDaemonAlignment with the composePreviewDaemon value to set, and it is set on the same PR, so a daemon change never automerges unseen. Tracked aggressively and automerged once CI is green: the release moves several times a day and the pin is only useful if it keeps up. Republishing the catalog against the new renderer needs no extra step, because design-artifacts.yml has a push trigger on main covering the manifest paths this PR touches.

LAST: re-enables the ONE compose-ui-builder coordinate this catalog versions, its BOM, after the rule above disabled every ee.schimke.composeai module. It is published from yschimke/compose-ui-builder on a release line of its own and resolves the test-only UI-builder exporter (`composeUiBuilder` in gradle/libs.versions.toml), so it moves on its own, independent of the plugin, and in its own group (the shared preset's `compose-ui-builder`). Automerged like its neighbour; `WearScreenTemplateRoundTripTest` is what catches an exporter change.
